title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: Equiatomic blend of Cr, Fe, V, W with either Ta or Ti added (forming CrFeVWTa or CrFeVWTi compositions)
recollection.intervention: Combination of first-principles/CALPHAD or MC simulations to evaluate phase stability, followed by experimental arc-melting and annealing, with XRD and SEM/EDS characterization
recollection.structure: Mainly BCC solid-solution high-entropy alloy, with possible minor Laves or σ phases precipitating after annealing, depending on whether Ta or Ti is used
recollection.mechanism: High configurational entropy favors single BCC phase; atomic-size mismatch and enthalpy terms modulate stability, with Ta promoting BCC over σ while Ti shifts toward Laves formation
recollection.results: Computations predict single-phase BCC stable above ~1100 °C; experiments find >90 % BCC for Ta alloy and ~70 % BCC + 30 % Laves for Ti alloy after annealing at 1000 °C; hardness ~450–500 HV for Ta alloy and ~520 HV for Ti alloy; CALPHAD and XRD data show good agreement within ±10 % phase fraction

score.note: The recollection misidentifies the computational and experimental methods: the paper used MD/hybrid MD-MC, mechanical alloying, and SPS rather than first-principles/CALPHAD, arc melting, and annealing. It correctly recalls broadly bcc-based structures and possible secondary phases, but wrongly assigns Laves formation to the Ti alloy; Fe2Ta C14 formed in the Ta alloy, while the Ti alloy had two bcc-type phases. The entropy/size/enthalpy mechanism is generic, and its composition-specific claims are incorrect. All reported temperatures, phase fractions, and hardness values are unsupported; it also omits the actual lattice parameters, density, segregation trends, and thermal diffusivity of roughly 3.5–7 mm²/s.
